plan.plan:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: MESSAGE QUEUE CAPACITY PLAN (APACHE KAFKA / SELF-MANAGED BROKER CLUSTER)

ASSUMPTIONS (documented because no project docs exist):
- Technology: Apache Kafka-compatible broker cluster (self-managed on cloud VMs or MSK-compatible). Justification: per-broker pricing is explicit and partitioned scaling maps directly to throughput.
- Message definition: 2.0 KB payload + 0.5 KB Kafka record overhead = 2.5 KB per message.
- Retention: 7 days on disk (time-based retention).
- Latency target: p99 end-to-end < 500 ms; operations thresholds enforce this via message-age alerts.
- Availability / durability: RF = 3, min.insync.replicas = 2, acks = all, 3 AZ deployment.
- Redundancy / broker count: 3 brokers minimum (1 per AZ) to satisfy RF=3.
- Burst allowance duration: 15 minutes (900 s) sustained; plan sizes for sustained burst, not just spike.
- Capacity methodology: Per-broker CPU, memory, network, disk I/O; aggregate cluster sized by partitioned load.
- Utilization targets: < 60% CPU/memory at 4,200 msg/s peak; < 85% at 12,600 msg/s burst.

STEP 1 — MESSAGE MODEL & THROUGHPUT MATH (used in all sections)
- Peak cluster throughput: 4,200 msg/s.
- Burst cluster throughput: 4,200 * 3 = 12,600 msg/s.
- Per-broker leader load (even partition spread): 4,200 / 3 = 1,400 msg/s at peak; 12,600 / 3 = 4,200 msg/s at burst.
- Replication overhead (RF=3): each broker also replicates ~2/3 of traffic, so total broker processing at burst ≈ 4,200 (leader) + 8,400 (follower/replication) = 12,600 msg/s equivalent per broker.
- Byte rates (aggregate ingress):
  - Peak: 4,200 msg/s * 2.5 KB = 10.5 MB/s.
  - Burst: 12,600 msg/s * 2.5 KB = 31.5 MB/s.
- Per-broker byte rate at burst ≈ 31.5 MB/s aggregate / 3 + replication mix ≈ 21–25 MB/s per broker, well under 10 Gbps (~1,250 MB/s).

STEP 2 — SIZING SECTION (compute / memory / storage / network)
Broker instance (per broker, 3 total):
- Compute: 16 vCPU / 64-core physical, 128 GB RAM (e.g., AWS r6i.4xlarge or equivalent). Justification: 4,200 msg/s per broker equivalent requires ~12–14 vCPU at peak load; 128 GB supports 32 GB heap + 96 GB page cache / OS buffers for 7-day retention windows and burst buffering.
- Network: 10 Gbps NIC (instance default); estimated 25 MB/s at 12,600 msg/s burst = 2% of link; headroom for replication and client fetch.
- Storage (per broker): 8 TB gp3 EBS (provisioned 16,000 IOPS / 1,000 MB/s throughput). Justification: 7-day retention math below.
- Aggregate cluster: 3 brokers, 48 vCPU / 384 GB RAM, 24 TB raw disk, 30 Gbps aggregate network.

Storage sizing derivation (consistency check):
- Unique data per day: 4,200 msg/s * 2.5 KB * 86,400 s = 907 GB/day ≈ 885 GiB/day.
- 7-day unique: 885 * 7 = 6,195 GB ≈ 6.2 TB.
- With RF = 3: 6.2 TB * 3 = 18.6 TB aggregate disk.
- Per broker share (even spread + replicas): ~6.2 TB base + 20% compaction/log overhead = 7.4 TB; rounded to 8 TB per broker.
- At 12,600 msg/s burst sustained for 15 min: additional transient 6.2 TB * (12,600/4,200 - 1) * (15/1440) ≈ negligible on 8 TB; buffer remains > 30%.

STEP 3 — COST SECTION (per broker, USD, monthly On-Demand rates, US East approximate)
Per-broker line items (must match 3-broker aggregate):
- Compute (r6i.4xlarge On-Demand): ~$0.80/hr * 730 hr = $584/mo.
- Storage (8 TB gp3 @ $0.08/GB-mo): 8,000 GB * 0.08 = $640/mo.
- Provisioned IOPS / throughput premium: 16,000 IOPS and 1,000 MB/s over gp3 base ≈ $100/mo.
- Cross-AZ replication / egress (est. 5 TB/mo per broker @ blended rates): ~$150/mo.
- Per-broker total: $584 + $640 + $100 + $150 = $1,474/mo → rounded to $1,500/mo for planning.
- Aggregate 3-broker cluster: 3 * $1,500 = $4,500/mo.
- Burst allowance justification (consistency): 12,600 msg/s requires the 16 vCPU / 128 GB / 8 TB spec; a smaller broker (e.g., 4 vCPU / 32 GB / 2 TB) would fail at burst. The $1,500/broker price buys headroom for the 3x burst, not just 4,200 msg/s.

STEP 4 — OPERATIONS SECTION (monitoring, alert thresholds, consistency)
Metrics monitored (per broker and cluster aggregate):
- CPU utilization % (per broker)
- Memory utilization % (per broker, JVM heap + system)
- Disk I/O utilization % / await / MB/s (per broker)
- Queue depth (messages per partition / aggregate; derived from log-end-offset - consumer-offset)
- Message age / consumer lag (seconds behind latest; derived from Kafka consumer lag metrics)
- Network utilization % (broker NIC)
- Message throughput (msg/s per broker and aggregate) — must track 4,200 and 12,600 explicitly.

Alert thresholds (explicitly reference 4,200 msg/s peak and 12,600 msg/s burst):
- CPU Warning: > 55% (indicates per-broker load exceeding ~1,400 msg/s / 4,200 msg/s aggregate peak; requires scaling investigation before burst).
- CPU Critical: > 85% (indicates per-broker load approaching ~4,200 msg/s / 12,600 msg/s aggregate burst; immediate scale or throttle required).
- Memory Warning: > 75%; Critical: > 92%.
- Disk I/O util Warning: > 70%; Critical: > 85% (compaction + replication at 12,600 msg/s can spike disk).
- Queue depth (aggregate): Warning > 50,000 messages (~12 s at 4,200 msg/s; ~4 s at 12,600 msg/s); Critical > 250,000 messages.
- Message age / lag: Warning > 2 s (4x p99 500 ms target); Critical > 10 s (indicates backlog exceeding burst absorption).
- Network (broker): Warning > 40% of 10 Gbps (~400 MB/s, far above 25 MB/s burst, so this is a hardware-fault/replication-flood guard); Critical > 70%.
- Throughput rate alert (aggregate): Warning when sustained > 4,200 msg/s for > 5 min; Critical when sustained > 10,000 msg/s (approaching 12,600 msg/s burst ceiling) for > 2 min.

STEP 5 — VALIDATION / BURST TEST PROCEDURE
- Load test: Produce 12,600 msg/s for 15 minutes (burst duration assumption) against 3-broker cluster with RF=3.
- Check: CPU per broker stays < 85%, disk < 85%, memory < 92%, lag < 10 s, queue depth < 250,000.
- Confirm storage growth rate at 12,600 msg/s ≈ 31.5 MB/s * 900 s = ~28 GB transient; 8 TB broker has > 20% headroom after 7-day retention.
- Confirm cost model holds: 3 brokers * $1,500 = $4,500/mo; no hidden broker count change required.

STEP 6 — CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY CHECKLIST (required by request)
- Figure 4,200 msg/s appears in: sizing (peak load), cost (headroom justification for 16 vCPU/128 GB), operations (warning baseline / rate alert).
- Figure 12,600 msg/s appears in: sizing (burst load / 4,200 msg/s per broker), cost (3x burst justifies premium instance/storage), operations (critical CPU / rate alert / lag threshold context).
- Figure 2.5 KB / 2 KB message size appears in: sizing (throughput and storage math), operations (queue-depth to time conversion implicitly uses rate, but storage retention of 7 days uses 2.5 KB consistently).
- Figure 3 brokers / 3 AZ appears in: sizing (aggregate specs), cost (per-broker pricing multiplied by 3), operations (per-broker thresholds applied to 3 instances).
- Figure 7-day retention appears in: sizing (6.2 TB unique / 18.6 TB aggregate / 8 TB per broker), operations (disk I/O and storage growth alerts implicit).
- Figure $1,500/broker and $4,500 aggregate appear only in cost, but are derived from sizing spec (r6i.4xlarge + 8 TB gp3) so they are consistent with infrastructure choices.

DELIVERABLE: This plan is the implementation document. No external repository or build tool is required; the human engineer applies the 3-broker cluster spec, the $4,500/mo cost model, and the 4,200/12,600 msg/s alert thresholds directly to procurement and monitoring setup.
success_criteria: The sizing section specifies exactly 3 brokers (16 vCPU, 128 GB RAM, 8 TB gp3 each), calculates aggregate peak load at 4,200 msg/s, and calculates burst load at 12,600 msg/s with per-broker load of ~4,200 msg/s under burst.

The cost section lists a per-broker monthly estimate of approximately $1,500 USD and an aggregate 3-broker cluster cost of approximately $4,500 USD/month, with the 12,600 msg/s burst explicitly cited as the justification for the 16 vCPU / 128 GB / 8 TB specification.

The operations section defines CPU, memory, disk I/O, queue-depth, message-age, and throughput-rate alert thresholds that explicitly reference both 4,200 msg/s (warning/baseline) and 12,600 msg/s (critical/burst) in their descriptions.

All sections apply the identical message-size assumption of 2.5 KB per record (2 KB payload + 0.5 KB overhead) and 7-day retention, yielding 6.2 TB unique / 18.6 TB aggregate storage, with per-broker storage set to 8 TB to include 20% overhead.

The plan includes a 15-minute burst-duration assumption and validates via load-test procedure that 8 TB per broker and 128 GB RAM absorb 12,600 msg/s sustained without exceeding 85% CPU or 85% disk utilization.
